title: Senate Report: CIA Detention & Interrogation (2014)
summary: Five-year SSCI study of 6.3M+ pages of CIA records; 500+ page declassified executive summary. Findings: 'enhanced interrogation techniques' were not effective; the CIA gave extensively inaccurate information about the program to policymakers and the public; management was deeply flawed; the program was far more brutal than represented (waterboarding, systematic beatings, sleep deprivation; 119+ detainees in secret 'black sites').
tldr: The Senate Intelligence Committee's five-year review found the CIA's 'enhanced interrogation' program was ineffective, built on false claims to policymakers, deeply mismanaged — and far more brutal than the CIA admitted, with sleep deprivation up to 180 hours and a detainee dying of suspected hypothermia.
ai_summary:
AI review of the Senate Intelligence Committee release on the CIA detention and interrogation program (Dec 9, 2014, via GlobalSecurity.org), read in full:
- Scope: review initiated March 5, 2009 (14–1 bipartisan vote); staff examined more than 6.3 million pages of CIA records over 3.5 years; study approved December 13, 2012 (9–6); declassification vote April 3, 2014 (11–3). It covers the secret overseas detention of at least 119 individuals, "in some cases amounting to torture."
- Not effective: the techniques "never" produced imminent-threat "ticking time bomb" intelligence; all 20 of the CIA's most-touted counterterrorism "successes" attributed to the program were "wrong in fundamental respects" — the information was either obtained before the techniques were used or was already available from other sources.
- Deception: the CIA provided inaccurate information to "the White House, Congress, the Justice Department, the CIA inspector general, the media, and the American public" — including falsely telling the Justice Department's Office of Legal Counsel that no senators had objected, when McCain, Feinstein, Hagel, Wyden, and Feingold had.
- Mismanagement: two outside contract psychologists with no interrogation experience (ex-Air Force SERE school) developed the techniques; their firm was paid more than $80 million; at least 26 of 119 detainees were wrongfully held; in November 2002 a detainee died of suspected hypothermia at the COBALT facility, held "partially nude and chained to a concrete floor."
- Brutality: sleep deprivation "for up to 180 hours," detainees told they would only leave in "a coffin-shaped box," Abu Zubaydah left "completely unresponsive with bubbles rising through his open full mouth" during waterboarding, KSM's waterboarding described internally as a "series of near drownings," and at least five detainees subjected to "rectal feeding" or "rectal hydration" without documented medical need.
- Record summary verified accurate against the document.
